subject: modelFit() function: Calculation of the parameters of fit

messages.author: dc001287bcd221ab
messages.subject: modelFit() function: Calculation of the parameters of fit
parts:
Dear All,

Thank you for letting me join this group.

I am interested in using the modelFit() function with fsQCA.
In making my first experiences with the function, I encountered two questions that I would like to ask. I attached an MRE to illustrate my questions.
  1. The function modelFit() returns parameters of fit (POF) for all intersections between a solution model (M) and theory (T) (M*T, M*~T, ~M*T, ~M*~T).
    --> How are the parameters of fit (POF) calculated for ~M*T?

    It is surprising to me that ~M*T (ABCE)  returns high inclusion (0.926) and PRI scores (0.760) since the resulting configuration (ABCE) is only reflected by the theory but not by the empirical solution.
    In the truth table (tt_present) the POF for ABCDE (incl = 0.892, PRI = 0.717) and ABC~DE (incl = 0.922, PRI = 0.667) are below the applied threshold criteria.

  2. When analyzing the solution of a negated outcome (i.e., ~Z), the function modelFit() throws an error:
    [.data.frame`(model$tt$initial.data, , model$tt$options$outcome) : undefined columns selected
    --> Is this error thrown because the function searches for the column name “~Z” instead of “Z”?

    If I negate the value of column Z and rename it to ~Z before running the function, everything works as expected.
Your support is very much appreciated!

Thank you and all the best
Marco

messages.author: a98c47479ea6b61f
messages.subject: Re: [QCA] modelFit() function: Calculation of the parameters of fit
parts:
Hello Marco,

The procedure in the modelFit() is rather simple:
- calculate the intersection between model and theory (with all combinations of presence and negations)
- then calculate the parameters of fit for the resulting expression

For the specific case of ~M*T, which is A*B*C*E, the inclusion score seems to be correct:

pof("A*B*C*E -> Z", data = CVF)
            inclS   PRI   covS   covU  
-------------------------------------- 
1  A*B*C*E  0.926  0.760  0.420    -   
-------------------------------------- 

This has nothing to do with the truth table configurations ABCDE and ABC~DE, since here we do not have the condition D.
If intersecting (taking the minimum fuzzy score) between conditions A, B, C and E, and then checking the sufficiency for the outcome, this is the result:

minint <- compute("A*B*C*E", data = CVF)
pof(minint, CVF$Z, relation = "sufficiency")
           inclS   PRI   covS   covU  
------------------------------------- 
1  minint  0.926  0.760  0.420    -   
------------------------------------- 

The configuration A*B*C*E is the result of the intersection between the negation of empirical solution and theory. Why it is the way it is, I can not say on the top of my head, but this is what the computer calculates (perhaps it deserves a more thorough investigation, it could be the subject of an entire paper).

Out of curiosity, I've tested your example against the function theory.evaluation() from package SetMethods, and still get a very high inclusion score, although the inclusion scores are not identical to my package (I think this needs to be checked in the package SetMethods, I am pretty sure the results in package QCA are correct).

Regarding the second point, I should definitely capture that error and add a more human readable message. You are quite right with the source of the error, if I remember correctly I have never thought of intersecting the minimization of the negation of the outcome with a theory.

It still makes little sense if I think about it, because the theory is about the presence of the outcome and not about its absence. Generally, the absence of something is extraordinarily heterogeneous (it can be absolutely anything), while only a few paths lead to producing an outcome. So having a theory about "anything else" in the Universe does not make much sense to me.

For the sake of the argument, if by "theory" of the negated outcome you mean the negation of your theoretical model, then your expression "~A*~B*~C" is not correct:

negate("A*B*C")
N1: ~A + ~B + ~C

because the negation of a conjunction is a disjunction.

But I should capture that error, that is for sure (thanks for reporting this).

Best, I hope this helps,
Adrian

messages.author: dc001287bcd221ab
messages.subject: Re: [QCA] modelFit() function: Calculation of the parameters of fit
parts:
Hello Adrian,

thank you for your extensive and very helpful answer!

While the POF for the intersection make sense to me now from a methodological point of view, I still struggle to grasp what it means for the interpretation of the results.
But your answer really helps to get a better understanding of how the POF are calculated for expressions such as the intersections between model and theory.

For illustration purposes, I used a random "theory" (~A*~B*~C) for the negated outcome, but I agree that simply negating theory for the presence of an outcome to predict the absence of an outcome does not make perfect sense. 
Thank you for clarifying this!

All the best
Marco
